first_impression.reaction: I searched for a template and the second sentence tells me I can have it with no sign-up. Good, no email wall, that's the usual catch. The download link is right there before any sales talk. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, then went back and checked the column list against the column count.

journey.quote: Ours downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up, opens in Google Sheets as well, and carries the travel columns a destination wedding needs: flights, arrival and departure, accommodation and visa letters.
journey.reaction: No sign-up is the first thing I check on any 'free template' page. Stated plainly, up front. Fine.

journey.section: Download the wedding guest list template
journey.quote: **Guest list** is where you work, with 36 columns grouped under headings in row 4.
journey.reaction: I counted the columns listed in the sections below and they add up to 36, and the destination group is eight as the takeaways say. Numbers that check out are worth more to me than adjectives.

journey.quote: Each cell takes Not invited, Invited, Attending or Declined.
journey.reaction: That's four options. Hold that thought.

journey.section: Excel and Google Sheets setup: Dropdowns
journey.quote: The four event columns offer the five reply options.
journey.reaction: Five? Earlier it listed four. Either there's a fifth option nobody told me about or someone didn't check. Small thing, but this is exactly how I decide whether the rest of a page has been checked.

journey.quote: Visa rules belong to each guest. Every guest should get the right visa for the countries they are visiting or transiting through, and check with the embassy or consulate of the destination before they travel, as [Smartraveller advises]
journey.reaction: Honest about where their responsibility ends and cites a government source. That's the kind of limitation statement I trust.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: And here's the pitch, halfway through a spreadsheet explainer. 'Anywhere in the world' and 'from start to finish' are claims with nothing behind them on this page. Who pays the Advisor, me or the venue? It doesn't say.

journey.quote: Months later, this is the column you will be grateful for.
journey.reaction: Mild filler. Doesn't hurt much, doesn't tell me anything either.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated, sourced to the OAIC, and clear about its limits. This section is the most credible part of the page.

journey.section: When a spreadsheet stops being enough
journey.quote: [Wonderland Studio](/wonderland-studio) is our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs.
journey.reaction: So the template is the on-ramp to an app. That's fine if they say what the app costs. They don't. That's the catch I'm looking for.

journey.section: Planning the weekend around your guests
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before work begins is a real commitment, I'll give them that. But it tells me there is a fee, not how it's worked out or whether they also take a cut from suppliers.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated: flat, percentage of budget, or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland or the Advisor take commissions or mark-ups from venues and vendors, and is that disclosed?
Does Wonderland Studio cost anything, and is the guest data I put in it shared with anyone?
Is there a fifth reply option in the event dropdowns, or is it four?
Can I see a real destination wedding the Advisor planned, with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Sweeping service claim dropped mid-explainer with no evidence and no fee model. Reads like a CTA before the page has earned it.

turn_offs_found.quote: The four event columns offer the five reply options.
turn_offs_found.why: Contradicts the four options listed under Events. Errors like this make me doubt everything else.

would_share_with: My fiancee, as the working guest list file
Whoever on her side is chasing RSVPs, as a cut-down copy per the privacy section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-guest-list-template&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I'd click to look at the Concierge page for the fee model, not to enquire. Nothing on this page answers 'do you take a cut from the venue?', so I won't enquire from here.

top_3_changes: Fix the dropdown inconsistency. old: "The four event columns offer the five reply options." new: "The four event columns offer the same reply options listed under Events." (Writer/editor to confirm against the actual .xlsx which number is right.)

Tone down the unsupported mid-article claim. old: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish." new: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact."

Cut the filler line. old: "What arrived and from whom, then Yes once the note has gone. Months later, this is the column you will be grateful for." new: "What arrived and from whom, then Yes once the note has gone."
